summary: The note recounts a sixth-grade field trip led by science teacher Ms. Eliza Bennett of Sunnydale Middle School to the Green Earth Conservation Area on October 3, 2023. Through an ecologist's trail guidance, an ecotourism specialist's talk, and meetings with conservation volunteers, students connected classroom learning to real ecosystems and environmental stewardship. It highlights the benefits of experiential learning and the pledges and community involvement it inspires.
one_line: A sixth-grade field trip to the Green Earth Conservation Area shows how outdoor education and ecotourism foster environmental stewardship in students.
key_facts: Ms. Eliza Bennett, a science teacher at Sunnydale Middle School, led sixth graders on a field trip on October 3, 2023.
The destination was the Green Earth Conservation Area.
The note says Ms. Bennett joined the school district in September 2024, which conflicts with the 2023 trip date.
Ecologist Mr. Alexei Petrov guided the group along trails, stressing that 'Every plant, every animal has a role in maintaining this balance.'
Student Miranda Jenkins was struck by how a pollinating bee can have a big impact.
Before the trip, students did a class project on native species and their habitats.
Student Omar learned about plastic pollution in rivers through a classroom simulation the week before, then saw the importance of clean water for wildlife on site.
Ecotourism specialist Lisa Chang defined ecotourism as responsible travel to natural areas that conserves the environment and sustains the well-being of local people.
Lisa Chang showed the students solar panels that power the on-site research facilities.
David, a former student of Ms. Bennett's, volunteers on weekends in habitat restoration and met with the students.
The group observed areas undergoing rehabilitation and discussed habitat degradation, renewable energy and conservation around protected areas.
Ms. Bennett has seen increased student interest in environmental clubs, science fairs and community service, including recycling programs and school garden projects.
Students made pledges afterward, such as picking up trash in their neighborhood and asking parents to plant more trees.
